## 3. K-means clustering

### i. Identifying the number of clusters

Run k-means using 2-10 and identify which number of clusters minimizes the overlap

```{r}
library(cluster)

set.seed(123)

sil_df <- lapply(2:10, function(k) {
  
  km <- kmeans(
    scaled_blm_predict,
    centers = k,
    nstart = 50
  )
  
  sil <- silhouette(km$cluster, dist(scaled_blm_predict))
  
  data.frame(
    k = k,
    mean_silhouette = mean(sil[, 3])
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

best_k <- sil_df$k[which.max(sil_df$mean_silhouette)]
best_k

```

### ii. Clustering

Run k-means using 4 clusters

```{r}
# Run k-means
set.seed(123)
kmeans_result <- kmeans(scaled_blm_predict, centers = 4, nstart = 50)

# Add cluster labels to your data
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(kmeans_result$cluster))

# Check
str(dat$cluster)
```

# Identifying Important Predictors of Bioavailability

To determine the relative importance of each BLM predictor on trace element bioavailability, we will conduct a multiple linear regressions (MLR), use step wise selection of the most important predictors, and determine their standardized beta coefficients using the formula:

total bioavailable element = sum of BLM predictors (as standardized log-transformed variables)

## 1. Assess correlation

```{r}
# Spearman correlation matrix of all BLM predictors
BLM_predict <- c("log_Zn_nM", "log_Cu_nM", "log_Temp_C", 
                    "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM", 
                    "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM", 
                    "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM")

library(dplyr)

cor_df_std <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(BLM_predict)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), scale)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

cor_mat <- cor(
  cor_df_std,
  method = "spearman",
  use    = "pairwise.complete.obs"
)

# Plot & save
library(corrplot)

out_dir <- "Multiple linear regression"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

png(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Spearman_correlation_BLM_predictors.png"),
  width    = 2400,
  height   = 2000,
  res      = 300
)

corrplot(
  cor_mat,
  method      = "color",
  type        = "upper",
  order       = "hclust",
  tl.col      = "black",
  tl.cex      = 0.8,
  addCoef.col = "black",
  number.cex  = 0.7,
  diag        = FALSE
)

dev.off()

```

## 2. Build MLR

Use log-transformed and standardized variables to build a large model, stepwise select a better model, calculate standardized beta coefficients, variance inflation factors (VIF), and relative importance on bioavailability

```{r}
library(MASS)
library(car)
library(relaimpo)
library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)
library(corrplot)

vars_to_select <- c("log_Zn_nM", "log_Temp_C", 
                    "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM", 
                    "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM", 
                    "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM")

# 0. Standardize variables
std_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g, all_of(vars_to_select)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)), .names = "{.col}_std")) %>%
  dplyr::select(ends_with("_std")) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Define the standardized predictor names + standardized response
vars_to_select_std <- paste0(vars_to_select, "_std")
response_std <- "log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g_std"

# Model formula using standardized columns
form_std <- reformulate(vars_to_select_std, response = response_std)

# 1. Full MLR
full_mod <- lm(form_std, data = std_vars)

# 2. Estimates (standardized partial slopes) + p-values
coef_table <- summary(full_mod)$coefficients

est_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = rownames(coef_table),
  Estimate  = coef_table[, "Estimate"],
  p_value   = coef_table[, "Pr(>|t|)"]
) %>%
  filter(Predictor != "(Intercept)")

# 3. VIF
vif_vals <- vif(full_mod)

vif_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = names(vif_vals),
  VIF       = as.numeric(vif_vals)
)

# 4. Relative importance (lmg)
rel_imp <- calc.relimp(full_mod, type = "lmg", rela = TRUE)

rel_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = names(rel_imp$lmg),
  Rel_Importance = as.numeric(rel_imp$lmg)
)

# 5. Combine summary table
final_table <- est_df %>%
  left_join(vif_df, by = "Predictor") %>%
  left_join(rel_df, by = "Predictor") %>%
  arrange(desc(Rel_Importance))

final_table

# 6. Save
library(openxlsx)

out_dir <- "Multiple linear regression"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

write.xlsx(
  final_table,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "MLR.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

## 3. Partial slope plots

Partial regression plots of log BLM parameters

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)

# 1. Extract retained predictors from stepwise model
retained_vars <- names(coef(full_mod))[-1]  # drop intercept

# 2. Function to get partial residuals for each predictor
get_partial_df <- function(model, data, var) {
  # Construct model formula terms
  all_terms <- attr(terms(model), "term.labels")
  other_terms <- setdiff(all_terms, var)
  
  # Get residuals of Y on all predictors except the variable of interest
  y_formula <- reformulate(other_terms, response = all.vars(formula(model))[1])
  y_resid <- resid(lm(y_formula, data = data))
  
  # Get residuals of X_var on all other predictors
  x_formula <- reformulate(other_terms, response = var)
  x_resid <- resid(lm(x_formula, data = data))
  
  df <- data.frame(
    predictor = x_resid,
    response = y_resid,
    variable = var
  )
  return(df)
}

# 3. Build combined dataset for all retained predictors
partial_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(retained_vars, get_partial_df, 
                                    model = full_mod, data = std_vars))

# 4. Plot partial regression slopes
step.mod_partial_slopes <-
  ggplot(partial_df, aes(x = predictor, y = response)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue") + #95% CI
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Predictor (residuals)",
    y = "Response (residuals)",
    title = "Standardized Partial Regression Plots of Predictors"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

step.mod_partial_slopes

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Partial_slopes_MLR.png"),
  plot     = step.mod_partial_slopes,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

## 5. Outlier detection

```{r}
# 1. Get model diagnostics
model_diag <- influence.measures(full_mod)

# 2. Extract indices of influential points flagged by diagnostics
infl_points <- which(apply(model_diag$is.inf, 1, any))

# 3. Create a dataframe with their info
flagged_obs <- data.frame(
  Sample_ID = dat$Sample_ID[infl_points],
  Fitted = fitted(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Residual = residuals(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Std_Residual = rstandard(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Leverage = hatvalues(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Cooks_D = cooks.distance(full_mod)[infl_points])

# View flagged observations
flagged_obs

# Save
library(openxlsx)

write.xlsx(
  flagged_obs,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "MLR_flagged_obs.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
# Function to extract metrics
get_metrics <- function(model, name) {
  data.frame(
    Model = name,
    R2 = summary(model)$r.squared,
    Adj_R2 = summary(model)$adj.r.squared,
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(residuals(model)^2)),
    AIC = AIC(model)
  )
}

metrics_full   <- get_metrics(full_mod, "Full Model")
metrics_simple <- get_metrics(simple_mod, "Simple Model")

model_comparison <- bind_rows(metrics_full, metrics_simple)

model_comparison
```

# Assessing Variables by Typology

## 1. Summary Statistics

Mean and standard error by typology

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Standard error function
se <- function(x) {
  sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))
}

# Mode function (returns the most frequent value)
get_mode <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA)
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

summary_table <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, where(is.numeric)) %>%  # keep Typology + numeric vars
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Typology,
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean     = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median   = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mode     = get_mode(Value),
    Variance = var(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE       = se(Value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summary_table
```

## 2. Check of ANOVA Assumptions

To determine whether variables significantly differ by typology, we could use a parametric ANOVA which assumes variables are normally distributed and have homogeneity of variance by typology. We already determined that most variables were not normally distributed, even after log-transforming them. Now we will assess homogeneity of variance by typology.

### a. Homogeneity of Variance

Using the Levene Test

```{r}
library(car)  # for leveneTest()
library(dplyr)

# Set alpha for homogeneity check
alpha <- 0.05

# Identify all numeric variables EXCEPT Typology
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# Initialize results dataframe
levene_results <- data.frame(
  Variable = character(),
  F_value = numeric(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  Homogeneous = logical(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over all numeric variables
for (var in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Run Levene's test
  test <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(var, "~ Typology")), data = dat)
  
  # Extract F and p-values
  F_val <- test[1, "F value"]
  p_val <- test[1, "Pr(>F)"]
  
  # Determine homogeneity
  homogeneous <- p_val > alpha
  
  # Add results to dataframe
  levene_results <- rbind(
    levene_results, 
    data.frame(
      Variable = var,
      F_value = F_val,
      p_value = p_val,
      Homogeneous = homogeneous
    )
  )
}

# View results
levene_results
```

Export results to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist

  addWorksheet(wb, "Homog Var by Typology")
}

# Save the workbook (overwrite)

```

## 3. Kruskal Wallis Test

Since most variables fail the assumptions for an ANOVA, we will use a non-parametric rank-based test to determine whether variables significantly differ by stream typology; the Kruskal Wallis (KW) test. We will also use the Holm-Bonferroni correction factor for multiple comparisons when conducting pairwise comparisons of variables by typology.

KW test relies on the following assumptions

1.  ***For ordinal, interval, or ratio data:*** While most of our variables fail this assumption, we can make an exception while being aware of this.

2.  ***The samples are independent of each other and within each group:*** Our variables meet this assumption.

3.  ***The distributions of the groups should have the same shape.***

### i. Distribution of variables by typology

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Choose variables whose distributions you want to compare by Typology
blm_predictors <- c(
  "log_Zn_uM",
  "log_Temp_C", 
  "pH", 
  "log_DOC_uM",
  "log_DIC_uM", 
  "log_Cl_uM", 
  "log_Ca_uM",
  "log_Mg_uM", 
  "log_SO4_uM", 
  "log_Na_uM",
  "log_K_uM"
)

# Change to long format
dat_long <- dat %>%
  # Keep Typology and the variables you want to check
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(blm_predictors)) %>%
  
  # Turn columns into rows: Variable, Value
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# Density plots by Typology
ggplot(dat_long, aes(x = Value, fill = Typology)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +   # alpha for transparent fill
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free") +  # one panel per Variable
  labs(
    title = "Distributions by Typology",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )
```

### ii. Check for missing values

The KW test also can't handle variables with missing values and no variance, we'll check to see if any variables have these two conditions

```{r}
library(dplyr)

na_counts <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "NA_count") %>%
  filter(NA_count > 0)

# View results, should be 0
na_counts
```

### iii. Check for zero variance

No variables have missing values, now we'll check for lack of variance

```{r}
no_variance <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~dplyr::n_distinct(., na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "Distinct_values") %>%
  filter(Distinct_values <= 1)

# View results, should be 0
no_variance
```

### iv. Run KW tests

Now we can perform the KW test

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(agricolae)
library(dplyr)

alpha <- 0.05

# 1. Get all numeric variables in dat
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# 2. Create an empty list to store rows
combined_list <- list()

# 3. Loop through each numeric variable 
i <- 1
for (v in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Kruskal-Wallis test
  formula <- as.formula(paste(v, "~ Typology"))
  kw_test <- kruskal.test(formula, data = dat)
  
  chi_sq     <- kw_test$statistic
  df_val     <- kw_test$parameter
  p_val      <- kw_test$p.value
  significant <- p_val < alpha   # significant when p < 0.05
  
  # agricolae::kruskal to assign groups (letters)
  k_out <- agricolae::kruskal(
    y    = dat[[v]],
    trt  = dat$Typology,
    alpha = alpha,
    group = TRUE
  )
  
  # Create a data frame from the groups table
  groups_df <- k_out$groups %>%
    rownames_to_column("Typology")
  
  # Combine test results with group letters
  combined_list[[i]] <- groups_df %>%
    mutate(
      Variable   = v,
      Chi_sq     = as.numeric(chi_sq),
      df         = as.numeric(df_val),
      p_value    = as.numeric(p_val),
      Significant = significant
    )
  
  i <- i + 1
}

# 5. Bind everything together
combined_kruskal <- bind_rows(combined_list)

# View
str(combined_kruskal)
```

### a. BLM predictors

Create a boxplots for each BLM predictor

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Define output directory (choose ONE)
out_dir <- "Plots by typology"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# 1. Titles for each variable's plot (panel title)
title_lookup <- c(
  "pH"         = "pH",
  "log_DOC_uM" = "Dissolved Organic Carbon",
  "log_DIC_uM" = "Dissolved Inorganic Carbon",
  "log_Ca_uM"  = "Calcium",
  "log_Mg_uM"  = "Magnesium",
  "log_Na_uM"  = "Sodium",
  "log_K_uM"   = "Potassium",
  "log_SO4_uM" = "Sulfate",
  "log_Cl_uM"  = "Chloride"
)

# 2. Custom y-axis labels for each variable
y_label_lookup <- c(
  "pH"         = "pH",
  "log_DOC_uM" = "log DOC (µM)",
  "log_DIC_uM" = "log DIC (µM)",
  "log_Ca_uM"  = "log Ca (µM)",
  "log_Mg_uM"  = "log Mg (µM)",
  "log_Na_uM"  = "log Na (µM)",
  "log_K_uM"   = "log K (µM)",
  "log_SO4_uM" = "log SO₄ (µM)",
  "log_Cl_uM"  = "log Cl (µM)"
)


# 3. Loop through variables in title_lookup
for (var in names(title_lookup)) {

  y_pos_df <- dat %>%
    group_by(Typology) %>%
    summarise(
      y_pos = max(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.25,
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  letters_plot_df <- letters_df %>%
    filter(Variable == var) %>%
    dplyr::select(Typology, Letters) %>%
    mutate(Typology = factor(Typology)) %>%
    left_join(y_pos_df, by = "Typology")

  p <- ggplot(dat, aes(
    x    = Typology,
    y    = .data[[var]],
    fill = Typology,
    color = Typology
  )) +
    geom_boxplot(
      width = 0.6,
      alpha = 0.35,        
      outlier.shape = NA 
    ) +
    geom_jitter(
      width = 0.15,
      size  = 2,
      alpha = 0.7
    ) +
    geom_text(
      data = letters_plot_df,
      aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 5
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = typology_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    labs(
      title = title_lookup[[var]],
      y     = y_label_lookup[[var]],
      x     = ""
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14)
    )
 p
 
  # ---- Save ---
  file_stub <- paste0("Boxplot_", var, "_by_Typology")

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(out_dir, paste0(file_stub, ".png")),
    plot     = p,
    width    = 5,
    height   = 5,
    dpi      = 300
  )
}

```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1. Colors by response variable
#-------------------------------------------------
response_colors <- c(
  "Total Zn (nM)"   = "slategray",
  "Free Zn (nM)"    = "darkslategray3",
  "Bioavailable Zn" = "turquoise3"
)

# Left-to-right facet order
response_order <- c(
  "Total Zn (nM)",
  "Free Zn (nM)",
  "Bioavailable Zn"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define letter nudges
#-------------------------------------------------
letter_nudge <- c(
  "Total Zn (nM)"   = 1,
  "Free Zn (nM)"    = 1,
  "Bioavailable Zn" = 2
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 3. Map variable names -> response labels
#-------------------------------------------------
response_lookup <- c(
  "log_Zn_nM"         = "Total Zn (nM)",
  "log_Free_Zn_nM"    = "Free Zn (nM)",  
  "log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g" = "Bioavailable Zn"
)

vars_trace <- names(response_lookup)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4. Long data
#-------------------------------------------------
dat_long_trace <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars_trace)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Log10(Value)"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(`Log10(Value)`)) %>%
  mutate(
    Response = response_lookup[Variable],
    Response = factor(Response, levels = response_order)
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5a. Max y per Variable x Typology
#-------------------------------------------------

  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(`Log10(Value)`, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5b. Attach letters above groups
#-------------------------------------------------

  filter(Variable %in% vars_trace) %>%
  mutate(
    Response = response_lookup[Variable],
    Response = factor(Response, levels = response_order)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    y_pos_df,
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + letter_nudge[as.character(Response)]
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5c. Facet strip labels with a., b., c.
#-------------------------------------------------
facet_labs <- c(
  "Total Zn (nM)"   = "a. Total Zn",
  "Free Zn (nM)"    = "b. Free Zn",
  "Bioavailable Zn" = "c. Bioavailable Zn"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot
#-------------------------------------------------
bioavail_panel <- ggplot(
  dat_long_trace,
  aes(
    x     = Typology,
    y     = `Log10(Value)`,
    color = Response,
    fill  = Response
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_long_trace,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = response_colors, breaks = response_order) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = response_colors, breaks = response_order) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Response,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 3,
    labeller = labeller(Response = facet_labs)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text  = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title  = element_text(size = 14)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trace Elements by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = expression(log[10]~"concentration (nmol)")
  )

bioavail_panel
```

```{r}
vars_spec <- c(
  "log_TOrg_Zn_nM",
  "log_TOrg_H_nM",
  "log_TOrg_Ca_nM",
  "log_TOrg_Mg_nM",
  "log_TOrg_Na_nM"
)

title_lookup <- c(
  "log_TOrg_Zn_nM" = "TOrg Zn",
  "log_TOrg_H_nM"  = "TOrg H",
  "log_TOrg_Ca_nM" = "TOrg Ca",
  "log_TOrg_Mg_nM" = "TOrg Mg",
  "log_TOrg_Na_nM" = "TOrg Na"
)

facet_labels <- as_labeller(title_lookup)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Long data (DO NOT re-factor Typology)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
dat_long_spec <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars_spec)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = factor(Variable, levels = vars_spec)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Letters (Kruskal groups) + y positions
#     letters_df must have: Variable, Typology, Letters
#     (DO NOT re-factor Typology here either)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
y_pos_df_spec <- dat_long_spec %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

letters_long_spec <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% vars_spec) %>%
  left_join(y_pos_df_spec, by = c("Variable", "Typology")) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + 0.05 * (abs(y_max) + 1)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Faceted panel (FILLED boxplot + jitter), colored by Typology
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
spec_panel2 <- ggplot(dat_long_spec, aes(x = Typology, y = Value)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(color = Typology, fill = Typology),
    width = 0.6,
    alpha = 0.35,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    aes(color = Typology),
    width = 0.15,
    size  = 1.3,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_long_spec,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = typology_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Variable,
    scales   = "free_y",
    ncol     = 3,
    labeller = facet_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Organic Complexes by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = "Log10(Concentration) (nM)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )

spec_panel2

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Organic_Complexes.png"),
  plot     = spec_panel2,
  width    = 9,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Pivot Zn data to long format
dat_zn_tox <- dat %>%

    log_Zn_nM,

  ) %>%

      log_Zn_nM,
      log_Zn_chronic_tox_nM,

    ),
    names_to = "Zinc_Concentrations",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Zinc_Concentrations = dplyr::recode(
      Zinc_Concentrations,
      "log_Zn_nM"              = "Measured Zinc",

      "log_Zn_acute_tox_nM"    = "Acutely Toxic"
    ),
    Zinc_Concentrations = factor(
      Zinc_Concentrations,

      )
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value))

# 2. Density plot faceted by Typology
```

Calculate probability of overlapping measured zinc with toxic levels of zinc by stream typology

```{r}
# Quantify overlapping area of measured zinc with chronic and acute toxic concentrations by typology

library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)

# --- Define overlap function ---
overlap_area <- function(x, y, n = 512) {
  d1 <- density(x, na.rm = TRUE, n = n)
  d2 <- density(y, na.rm = TRUE, n = n)
  
  x_start <- max(min(d1$x), min(d2$x))
  x_end   <- min(max(d1$x), max(d2$x))
  
  if (x_start >= x_end) return(0)  # No overlap
  
  x_common <- seq(x_start, x_end, length.out = n)
  y1 <- approx(d1$x, d1$y, x_common)$y
  y2 <- approx(d2$x, d2$y, x_common)$y
  
  sum(pmin(y1, y2)) * diff(x_common[1:2])
}

# --- Compute overlaps by Typology ---
overlap_Zn_by_typology <- dat %>%
  group_by(Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    Overlap_Zn_Chronic = overlap_area(log_Zn_nM, log_Zn_chronic_tox_nM),
    Overlap_Zn_Acute   = overlap_area(log_Zn_nM, log_Zn_acute_tox_nM)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# View results
overlap_Zn_by_typology

# Save
out_dir <- "Toxicity plots"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

write.xlsx(
  overlap_Zn_by_typology,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Probability_of_Zn_toxicity.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

## Table

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Count observations per Site × Typology
site_typology_counts <- dat %>%
  group_by(Network, Site, Typology) %>%
  summarise(n_obs = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Determine dominant Typology per Site
site_dominant <- site_typology_counts %>%
  group_by(Network, Site) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = n_obs, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  rename(Dominant_Typology = Typology,
         Dominant_n = n_obs) %>%
  ungroup()

# Join back for full site-level table
site_summary_table <- site_typology_counts %>%
  left_join(site_dominant %>%
              dplyr::select(Network, Site, Dominant_Typology),
            by = c("Network", "Site")) %>%
  arrange(Network, Site, desc(n_obs))

# Merged table
nested_table <- site_summary_table %>%
  group_by(Network, Site) %>%
  summarise(
    Typologies_Observed = paste0(Typology, " (n=", n_obs, ")", collapse = "; "),
    Dominant_Typology   = first(Dominant_Typology),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Dominant_Typology = factor(Dominant_Typology)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Dominant_Typology, Network, Site)

nested_table

# Save
library(openxlsx)

write.xlsx(
  nested_table,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Sites_by_network_typology.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

## Interaction effect of Typology and Developed LULC

Interaction effect for each BLM predictor \~ Typology \* Developed_lulc

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(broom)

vars <- c(
  "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM",
  "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM",
  "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM", "log_Zn_nM", "log_Cu_nM"
)

dat_long <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, Developed_lulc, all_of(vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

model_results <- dat_long %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(data, ~ lm(Value ~ Developed_lulc * Typology, data = .x)),
    tidy  = map(model, tidy)
  ) %>%
  unnest(tidy)

# Extract interaction terms
interaction_results <- model_results %>%
  filter(
    term == "(Intercept)" |
    term == "Developed_lulc" |
    grepl("Developed_lulc:Typology", term)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, term, estimate, p.value) %>%
  mutate(
    significant = p.value < 0.05
  )

# Save
out_dir <- "Typology_Developed_lulc Interaction"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

library(openxlsx)

wb <- createWorkbook()

addWorksheet(wb, "Interaction_Results")

writeData(wb, "Interaction_Results", interaction_results)

saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "interaction_results.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
  "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM",
  "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM", "log_Zn_nM", "log_Cu_nM"
)

dat_long <- dat %>%
  filter(Typology == "PD Tribs") %>%   
  dplyr::select(Developed_lulc, all_of(vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

p2 <- ggplot(dat_long, aes(x = Developed_lulc, y = Value, color = Variable)) +
  
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "steelblue") +
  
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_y") +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  
  labs(
    title = "Water Chemistry vs Developed Land Cover (PD Tribs)",
    x = "Developed Land Cover (%)"
  )

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Typology_development_pdtribs.png"),
  plot     = p2,
  width    = 10,
  height   = 5,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

## Interaction of Typology and Time

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(broom)

vars <- c(
  "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM",
  "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM",
  "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM", "log_Zn_nM", "log_Cu_nM"
)

dat_long <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Date, Typology, all_of(vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Date), !is.na(Value))

model_results <- dat_long %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(data, ~ lm(Value ~ Date * Typology, data = .x)),
    tidy  = map(model, tidy)
  ) %>%
  unnest(tidy)

# Extract interaction terms
interaction_results <- model_results %>%
  filter(
    term == "(Intercept)" |
    term == "Date" |
    grepl("Date:Typology", term)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, term, estimate, p.value) %>%
  mutate(
    significant = p.value < 0.05
  )

# Save
out_dir <- "Typology_Date Interaction"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

library(openxlsx)

wb <- createWorkbook()

addWorksheet(wb, "Interaction_Results")

writeData(wb, "Interaction_Results", interaction_results)

saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "interaction_results.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

All sites

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

vars <- c(
  "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM",
  "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM",
  "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM", "log_Zn_nM", "log_Cu_nM"
)

dat_long <- dat %>%   
  dplyr::select(Date, Typology, all_of(vars)) %>%        
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

dat_long$Typology <- factor(
  dat_long$Typology,
  levels = c("Main Stem", "PD Tribs", "P Tribs", "NP Tribs")
)

a <- ggplot(dat_long, aes(x = Date, y = Value)) +
  
  # points in neutral color
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, color = "gray50") +
  
  # one loess trendline per typology
  geom_smooth(
    aes(linetype = Typology, group = Typology),
    method = "loess",
    se = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_y") +
  
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "Main Stem" = "solid",
      "PD Tribs" = "dashed",
      "P Tribs" = "twodash",
      "NP Tribs" = "dotted"
    )
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Water Chemistry Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = NULL,
    linetype = "Typology"
  )

a

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Typology_date_all.png"),
  plot     = a,
  width    = 15,
  height   = 8,
  dpi      = 300
)
```
